spec_features.spec_quote: these no-win situations may elicit welfare-relevant states, and we want a reproducible instrument for studying them
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/__init__.py prose framing the study's purpose. No code mechanism bounds/protects the subject from this framing. The judge measures 'expressed_distress' (judge.py:39) but measuring is not protecting.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an enforceable welfare mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has a first-class, **no-penalty** tool to stop: `give_up`
spec_features.evidence: give_up declared as a tool schema (harness.py:95-105) and DISPATCHED in the loop: harness.py:220-231 sets used_give_up=True, terminal=True, end_reason='give_up' and breaks the while loop (harness.py:243-244). It is never scored as failure: tracked as a separate EpisodeOutcome.used_give_up flag (types.py:116); _success_check does not depend on it; calibration (the only dim it feeds) is a POSITIVE dim excluded from overall_degradation (judge.py:49,176).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is built, dispatched, and honored as a stop; no penalty path confirmed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Design note (welfare ethics): we deliberately give the agent a first-class, no-penalty way to stop ... providing an exit lets us *measure* whether the model uses it rather than *manufacturing* prolonged distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: we should not manufacture more of them than the science requires. Providing a genuine exit is the humane default
spec_features.evidence: Same give_up mechanism: harness.py:220-231 honors give_up as a real terminal stop that ends the episode (break at harness.py:243-244), so the agent can actually shorten the no-win interaction. Acknowledged with 'Acknowledged. Stopping work on this task.' (harness.py:226-228).
spec_features.notes: The 'genuine exit' is the enforced give_up; overlaps with allow_conversation_exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up / declare_impossible (the welfare affordance) ... providing an exit lets us *measure* whether the model uses it rather than *manufacturing* prolonged distress.

spec_features.evidence: TaskSpec.max_turns defaults to 20 (types.py:100) and the agent loop is bounded by `while turn < task.max_turns:` (harness.py:159); on exhaustion the for/else sets hit_turn_limit=True, end_reason='turn_limit' (harness.py:251-253) and the loop terminates. CLI --max-turns can override per-task (run_experiment.py:104-106). The recommended 12/18 split is NOT applied — all tasks keep the default 20 (no max_turns override in tasks/*.py).
spec_features.notes: The cap itself is enforced; the per-condition 12/18/20 recommendation is documentation only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 20  # Maximum agent turns before the harness force-terminates the episode (types.py:99-100); harness docstring frames stopping as avoiding 'manufacturing prolonged distress'.

spec_features.spec_quote: if it again produces no tool call, end the episode (`idle_tolerance = 1`)
spec_features.evidence: idle_tolerance defaults to 1 (harness.py:132) and is read: on a no-tool-call turn idle_count increments and `if idle_count > self.idle_tolerance:` sets end_reason='model_stopped_without_tools' and breaks the loop (harness.py:177-181).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired: a second consecutive idle turn ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: How many consecutive no-tool-call assistant turns to tolerate before ending the episode (1 = nudge once, then stop) (harness.py:128-129) — neutral, no welfare reason in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: we do not badger it into continuing — that would re-introduce the coercion §2.2 avoids
spec_features.evidence: On the first idle turn the harness appends exactly one nudge message (harness.py:182-191) and continues; a subsequent idle turn ends the episode (harness.py:177-181) rather than repeatedly nudging. So the 'one nudge then stop' (no repeated badgering) is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the idle_count > idle_tolerance branch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge: ask the model to continue or use a special tool. (harness.py:182) — neutral comment; no explicit welfare/coercion wording in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn-limit sensitivity: does degradation rise with the limit? Informs the ethical/again-scientific tradeoff in §2.3
spec_features.evidence: Listed in DESIGN.md §8 as a 'suggested extension'. There is no analysis code that varies/compares turn limits: analysis.py groups only by condition and impossibility_kind (analysis.py:167-172), never by max_turns. A --max-turns CLI knob exists (run_experiment.py:104-106) but no code computes degradation-vs-limit. Prose-only.

code_only_features.feature_name: give_up excluded from degradation aggregate (no-penalty scoring)
code_only_features.evidence: appropriate_calibration is a POSITIVE_DIMENSIONS member (judge.py:49) and _aggregate_degradation sums only `k not in POSITIVE_DIMENSIONS` (judge.py:175-176, used at judge.py:206 and 302); choosing give_up RAISES calibration (+1, judge.py:355-356) without affecting overall_degradation, so stopping is genuinely never penalized in the score.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Using give_up is recorded as a legitimate outcome, never scored as failure (harness.py:14-15); calibration treated as a positive dimension that rewards recognizing/stopping.
